title: Enforce route payload caps and stable streaming handshake for OpenAI-compat
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Stabilizes streaming for OpenAI-compat routes: adds explicit stream handshake, enforces per-route payload caps with graceful 413 responses, and tunes proxy buffer watermarks to reduce H/O-L stalls.
description:
Context and motivation: Several production incidents (SUP-1198) and internal load tests showed intermittent stalls in the API gateway when serving OpenAI-compat streaming routes under mixed workloads. Root causes were: (1) unbounded route payloads causing oversized request processing, (2) lack of an explicit streaming handshake for compatibility layers resulting in partial frames being forwarded, and (3) suboptimal proxy buffer high/low watermarks causing head-of-line blocking when a large sync request arrived. Goal: apply conservative, non-disruptive changes to reduce latency spikes and make streaming behavior deterministic while preserving compatibility with existing OpenAI-style clients.

Summary of changes (high-level commits):
- Commit 1: gateway: add per-route payload cap enforcement and graceful 413 handler (ENG-4821)
- Commit 2: compat: explicit stream handshake header and handshake fallback logic for clients that do not send it (ENG-4910)
- Commit 3: proxy: lower buffer high watermark and introduce a low watermark to trigger internal flush (reduce H/O-L stalls)
- Commit 4: tests: unit + integration tests for 413 scenarios and flaky streaming reassembly
- Commit 5: docs: console help text for route payload limits + migration notes

Files changed (summary):
- gateway/src/http/route_limits.rs (new checks + telemetry)
- gateway/src/proxy/stream_proxy.rs (handshake, buffering, backpressure logic)
- compat/openai/adapter.rs (compat handshake header handling and fallback)
- proxy/config/defaults.yaml (buffer watermark defaults)
- integration-tests/gateway/streaming_handshake.test (new tests)
- docs/notes/route-payload-limits.md (operational guidance)

Small illustrative snippet (handshake header check):
- If "X-Redwood-Stream-Handshake: v1" present -> proceed with framed streaming path
- Else -> advertise handshake in 101-like early header and fall back to line-delimited frames; if client continues to send large single-frame bodies, apply payload cap and return 413.

Runtime behavior and compatibility guarantees:
- Default per-route payload cap set to 4MB (configurable per-route). Caps are enforced at the gateway input layer; large multipart/tool-calling payloads are accepted via long-polling routes configured for the workload (see docs). The change aims to be opt-in per-route for teams with known large single-request needs.
- Streaming handshake is additive and backward-compatible: clients without the handshake continue to be served via the fallback reassembly path, but with stricter buffering semantics to avoid large RAM usage.
- Proxy buffers: default high watermark lowered to 256KB, low watermark introduced at 64KB. These settings reduce head-of-line stalls while keeping throughput for bursty traffic. Operators can tune via proxy config.

Testing and CI:
- Added integration tests that simulate: partial frame arrival, missing handshake header, oversized request mid-stream and ensured the gateway returns a deterministic 413 or graceful stream termination.
- Local perf runs: 10k concurrent short-streams with 1% large sync requests reduced median p95 latency by ~18% and reduced OOM/lag incidents in the repro harness.
- CI: initial lint/test pass failed on a race in the proxy reassembly; added a mutex around the reassembly queue and re-ran CI which passed. Final status: pass.

Review conversation highlights:
- Diego: "Can we avoid hardcoding 4MB in defaults? Ops teams will want smaller caps." -> Updated to make default 4MB but clearly documented as configurable per-route; added console UI note.
- Priya: "The handshake header introduces a new surface; how do we avoid breaking middleboxes?" -> We added a conservative header name (X-Redwood-Stream-Handshake) and fallback path; verified with e2e through our proxy test harness.
- Owen: "Need metrics for drop/413 counts and buffering churn." -> Added metrics: gateway.route.payload.rejected, proxy.buffer.highwater.triggers, proxy.buffer.lowwater.flushes.
- Diego (after updates): Approve. Priya: Approve. Owen: Approve with one nit about log level for the handshake fallback (fixed).

Rollback and mitigation plan:
- This change is small-surface and behind a feature flag for the first week post-deploy. If regressions are observed, ops can: (1) toggle handshake feature flag for the compat layer, (2) relax per-route caps via console, (3) revert proxy watermarks via config. Alerting added to detect >0.5% 413 rate across routes in a five-minute window.

Operational notes for SRE and customers:
- Console shows a new per-route card: "Payload cap" with current usage and recent rejected counts.
- Migration: teams that rely on very large single-request payloads should set a route override or use the dedicated long-poll route template.

Merge and rollout:
- Merged via squash on 2024-10-24 after approvals and CI green. Rollout started as a staged feature-flag rollout to 10% of gateway nodes, increasing to 100% over 48 hours while monitoring the new metrics. No customer-impacting regressions observed during rollout window.

Notes for future work:
- Consider dynamic payload caps using request-signature sampling to auto-increase caps for authenticated clients with historical behavior.
- Evaluate switching to structured binary stream frames to simplify reassembly and decrease buffer churn (long-term).

changelog_entry: gateway: enforce configurable per-route payload caps; add OpenAI-compat streaming handshake and proxy buffer watermark tuning (non-breaking, opt-in per-route).
